title: RKLB Stock Rises Overnight: Cathie Wood’s ARK Sees ‘Enormous Opportunity’ As SpaceX Eyes Falcon 9 Retirement
body: ARK bought about 233,482 Rocket Lab shares worth $16.6 million last week across ARKK, ARKQ and ARKX.Falcon 9 is reportedly fully booked until 2028 or 2029 for some customers; its retirement depends on Starship achieving reliable, frequent flights.Neutron’s readiness remains key, while Rocket Lab’s proposed $8 billion Iridium acquisition would add a satellite fleet and spectrum.Shares of Rocket Lab (RKLB) rose 0.3% overnight heading into Tuesday as Cathie Wood’s ARK Investment Management said SpaceX’s upcoming shift away from Falcon 9 could create an “enormous opportunity” for rival launch providers.RKLB stock declined 1% on Monday to $73.02, snapping two straight sessions of gains. ARK Bets On RKLB With A Launch BottleneckARK analysts Tasha Keeney and Daniel Maguire said that a U.S. launch bottleneck could emerge if SpaceX scales Starship toward 10,000 annual flights by 2030, mostly for StarMind orbital data centers, and retires Falcon 9 by the decade’s end.That could create an “enormous opportunity” for Rocket Lab and Stoke Space to capture share, they said, “should their medium-lift rockets deliver.” Multiple providers would support the U.S. government’s preference for a diversified supply chain and offer alternatives to communications, cloud and AI companies unwilling to rely on SpaceX for launch. The analysis followed Starship Flight 14, which reached orbit and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites despite an engine shutdown. ARK estimated the added capacity could support nearly $560 million in annualized revenue. ARK also sees full reusability potentially lowering launch costs to $100 per kilogram or less at scale, improving orbital data-center economics. Flight 15’s upper-stage catch is the next major test.Meanwhile, ARK bought about 233,482 Rocket Lab (RKLB) shares worth $16.6 million last week, comprising $12.6 million in the ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK), $2.9 million in the ARK Autonomous Technology & Robotics ETF (ARKQ) and $1.1 million in the ARK Space Exploration & Innovation ETF (ARKX). The buying extends ARK’s return to the stock after earlier sales, including exits from ARKQ and ARKX in June. It also bought about $25.7 million across the three funds last month. SpaceX Customers Face Launch CrunchAt least seven spacecraft companies have reportedly been told Falcon 9 is fully booked until 2028 or 2029. Starlink’s share of its missions has risen from 54% in 2020 to about 79% in 2026. Some customers have apparently struggled to secure flights after 2028 as SpaceX winds down shared launches.Musk has tied Falcon’s phaseout to Starship reliably flying several times a week, rather than a fixed retirement date. Government missions could keep Falcon operating into the early 2030s.Rocket Lab’s Next Leap Depends On NeutronMeanwhile, Rocket Lab secured its largest commercial Electron agreement last week: 20 dedicated Synspective launches scheduled from 2028 through 2031. The deal brings Synspective’s contracted Electron missions to 47 and Rocket Lab’s launch backlog above 100. Its Sept. 26 flight, the 97th Electron mission and 18th of 2026, deployed Synspective’s 13th StriX radar satellite. However, Capturing ARK’s medium-lift opportunity depends on Neutron, which has yet to generate launch revenue. Rocket Lab targeted fourth-quarter delivery to the pad, and has since said the window for a flight before year-end is narrowing.Rocket Lab’s proposed $8 billion Iridium Communications (IRDM) acquisition would also add a satellite fleet and spectrum. The deal is expected to close in mid-2027.How Do Retail Traders Feel About RKLB?On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for RKLB slipped to ‘bearish’ from ‘neutral’ levels a dat ago amid a 172% jump in 24-hour message volumes.RKLB sentiment and message volume as of October 6 | Source: StocktwitsOne user said, “$RKLB End to End hidden gem. title: Can Rocket Lab Capitalize on Falcon 9’s Exit Before Neutron Slips Again
body:
Space Exploration Technologies Corp.'s (NASDAQ:SPCX) decision to stop selling new Falcon 9 rideshare missions after 2028 creates the biggest opening in the medium-lift launch market in years; but Rocket Lab Corporation's (NASDAQ:RKLB) Neutron seems built to fill that gap. Its backlog suggests demand is already there. But capturing that opportunity depends on Neutron delivering on an unproven timeline. The rocket has yet to fly, has already suffered a delay tied to a hardware failure, and Rocket Lab has described its year-end launch window with increasing caution each quarter.

Despite the Falcon 9 news, SpaceX remains a top AI stock, as long as investors are wary of the one red-flag we pointed out in our previous coverage of the stock.

Falcon 9's Exit Creates an Opening for Rocket Lab

SpaceX has stopped selling new Falcon 9 rideshare missions, leaving some customers unable to secure flights beyond 2028 as the company shifts resources toward Starship. By contrast, Rocket Lab total backlog has grown to about $2.36 billion, including $940.2 million in launch services, while its launch backlog exceeds 90 missions. At least seven Neutron-specific launches for confidential commercial customers are already booked through 2029, leading CEO Peter Beck to say Neutron demand is not something he "sits awake at night worrying about." Neutron is designed for the same medium-lift segment Falcon 9 dominates today, while Electron can absorb some of the short-term overflow as the world's most frequently launched orbital small rocket.

Rocket Lab made our list of 10 stocks Reddit thinks could go to the moon—but nine stocks ranked ahead of it. See where RKLB landed and which names beat it.

The Catch: Neutron Still Has to Fly

A tank qualification failure that emerged unexpectedly in January 2026 has already delayed Neutron's first launch to the fourth quarter of 2026. Rocket Lab has since acknowledged in its own filings that the launch window is narrowing. With the stock trading at roughly 57 times trailing revenue while Neutron has yet to fly, much of the expected demand may already be reflected in the valuation. Rival Stoke Space, which is targeting the same market gap, has also delayed its debut from 2025 to 2027. The delay highlights how frequently new-rocket schedules can slip.

Rocket Lab Is Priced for a Smooth Neutron Launch

Rocket Lab's valuation suggests the market is already paying for a smooth Neutron ramp. The forward GAAP P/E isn't meaningful since the company is still loss-making. Its forward Price-to-sales ratio of 43.53x sits about 50% above its 5-year average of 29.03x, a steep premium to its historical norms. The EPS outlook shows why. Losses are expected to narrow in 2026, while 2028 estimates likely assume Neutron is flying regularly by the time the Falcon 9 rideshare gap opens. Those 2028 estimates likely assume Neutron is flying regularly by then, so another delay could push them back. The balance sheet is a clear strength. Rocket Lab holds $2.30 billion in cash against just $133.69 million in debt. In my view, near-perfect execution is largely priced in already.

Rocket Lab saw a notable increase in hedge fund ownership, with the number of funds holding the stock rising from 43 at the end of Q1 2026 to 52 at the end of Q2 2026. Short interest reached 7.6% of float as of August 31, 2026, compared with 5.4% since the stock's all-time high in May.

SpaceX has 119 hedge funds among its institutional holders, highlighting broad institutional interest. As of August 31, 2026, short interest accounted for 2.76% of float, a modest level that points to limited bearish positioning even as investors weigh whether Rocket Lab can capitalize on the Falcon 9 rideshare gap through Neutron.

The Falcon 9 opening and Neutron's backlog are both real. However, Rocket Lab only captures the full benefit on its own timeline if Neutron reaches orbit reliably. The program's recent delays leave that timeline far from settled.

While we acknowledge the potential of RKLB as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. title: SpaceX Gains 2% as Morgan Stanley Sees a Closing Window; AST SpaceMobile Surges 8%, Rocket Lab Rises 5%
body:
A single Morgan Stanley note on SpaceX just sent the entire commercial space sector surging, but the company at the center of the call posted the smallest gain of the group, raising questions about what investors are actually buying.

This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

Morgan Stanley’s case that Wall Street is underpricing the compute side of SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX | SPCX Price Prediction) is lifting the whole commercial space group, and the biggest gains are showing up outside the company at the center of the note. SpaceX stock is at $174.67, up 2% in morning trading, the smallest advance among the three space names in focus.

Also, AST SpaceMobile (NASDAQ:ASTS) stock is at $63.34, up 8%, the biggest gain of the group. Rocket Lab (NASDAQ:RKLB) stock is at $76.31, up 5%, landing in the middle of the pack.

For a sector-wide read, the Procure Space ETF (NASDAQ:UFO), a fund that counts all three names among its holdings, is up 2%. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 0.6%, a much softer gain for the broad market. Space stocks are drawing buying that runs well ahead of large-cap equities as a whole.

Morgan Stanley Flags a Narrow Window for SpaceX

Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Jonas repeated an Outperform rating on SpaceX stock with a $300 price target, arguing that investors have only a few weeks to act before the next Starship test flight. That Morgan Stanley note landed in the prior session, and the rally in SpaceX stock has carried into this one. Jonas built his case on a sum-of-the-parts argument, which values each SpaceX business separately and then adds those figures together.

In that framework, the market fully values the launch and satellite connectivity businesses at SpaceX while assigning little or nothing to the compute and chipmaking side. Jonas also argued that few investors can judge the testing path on a reusable upper stage or forecast compute pricing, which keeps many out.

AST SpaceMobile Leads on a Different Business Model

AST SpaceMobile is building a direct-to-device satellite network that connects ordinary mobile phones, putting it up against the Starlink side of SpaceX rather than the launch franchise behind the Morgan Stanley note. Posting the smallest gain of the three, SpaceX stock cuts against reading the move as a SpaceX-specific revaluation and points to the space complex rising together.

Late September delivered the milestone that frames the Morgan Stanley timeline, as SpaceX reached low Earth orbit for the first time on a Starship test flight and deployed Starlink satellites on that mission. SpaceX stock is up 18% over the past month, a stretch that includes that flight.

What to Watch Next

For SpaceX stock, the next catalyst is the upcoming Starship test flight, since the window argument from Jonas depends on that milestone landing on schedule. A slip could drain urgency from the Morgan Stanley case on SpaceX, while a clean flight could lend weight to the sum-of-the-parts view. A confirmed date for the next SpaceX Starship test is worth watching.

AST SpaceMobile stock and Rocket Lab stock are rising on enthusiasm triggered by a note about SpaceX. The focus shifts to whether AST SpaceMobile and Rocket Lab shares hold their gains once attention on the SpaceX call passes.

If the space-stock rally rests on one analyst’s thesis and a SpaceX test flight that’s still ahead, this leaves room for big price swings in either direction. Investors weighing their exposure should adjust their holdings carefully given how quickly AST SpaceMobile, Rocket Lab and SpaceX shares can wobble on sentiment alone.

title: Rocket Lab Just Gained 17% in a Month: Is It Too Late to Buy RKLB Stock Now?
body:
Rocket Lab just pulled off a rare feat by leaving the broader space sector in the dust, but three simultaneous high-stakes bets now sit between the company and the future its stock price already assumes.

Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.

This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

Space stocks split widely over the past month. Shares of Rocket Lab (NASDAQ:RKLB | RKLB Price Prediction) landed on the strong side alongside shares of SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX). However, shares of satellite network builder AST SpaceMobile (NASDAQ:ASTS) barely budged over the same stretch. That split points to company-specific stories behind the rally, which makes the move in Rocket Lab stock worth a closer look.

Rocket Lab stock is up 17% over the past month to $75.31. Similarly, SpaceX stock gained 17% over the past month to $172.72, leaving the two names moving together.

In contrast, AST SpaceMobile stock is up just 1% over the past month to $62.94, representing a fraction of the gains in Rocket Lab and SpaceX shares.

For sector context, the Procure Space ETF (NASDAQ:UFO) is up 1% over the past month. Checking on the broader market, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is also up 1% over the past month. With the space fund and the broad market both posting modest gains, the run in Rocket Lab and SpaceX shares stands out as a two-company event.

Iridium Deal Could Remake Rocket Lab

Rocket Lab has announced a deal to acquire Iridium Communications, a move that would make the company vertically integrated. Under that structure, Rocket Lab could design, build, launch and then operate its own satellite constellations delivering communications services globally. That combination would place Rocket Lab among the few space companies controlling every step from the factory floor to the paying customer.

Iridium follows two smaller acquisitions by Rocket Lab. The company bought Mynaric for laser communications and Motiv for space robotics, adding capabilities that feed directly into the spacecraft it builds. Each deal moves Rocket Lab closer to running a full-service space operation.

How Rocket Lab Makes Money

Rocket Lab flies the Electron small-lift rocket and the HASTE suborbital vehicle, and the company is developing the medium-lift reusable Neutron rocket. Satellites and spacecraft components built by Rocket Lab have flown on more than 1,700 missions in Earth orbit and in deep-space exploration. Such a record gives Rocket Lab proven flight heritage across both launch and hardware.

Revenue at Rocket Lab comes from products, meaning spacecraft and hardware, and from services, meaning launch, with commercial operators and major defense clients, including the U.S. Space Force, making up its customer base. Owning Iridium would add recurring fees from a satellite network that bills customers continuously, a sharp shift for a business currently paid once per launch.

Three Hard Jobs at Once

Execution is the main risk for Rocket Lab. The company is simultaneously buying a satellite operator in Iridium, building the Neutron rocket and folding Mynaric and Motiv into its operations, while any one of those jobs could stretch a management team and three together leave little room for delays.

Rocket Lab stock already reflects a version of events in which all three efforts work. After a 17% climb over the past month, Rocket Lab shares carry less buffer if Neutron is delayed or the Iridium integration proves costly. A blow on any front could weigh on the stock more heavily now than it would have a month ago.

What to Watch Next

Updates on the Iridium deal and Neutron development are worth watching, since both shape whether Rocket Lab becomes the vertically integrated operator its acquisitions point toward. Progress on either front carries more weight for Rocket Lab now that the stock has priced in a good outcome.

Investors weighing their exposure should adjust their holdings carefully given that Rocket Lab is managing an acquisition, a new rocket and two integrations at once. Share positions should reflect both the strength of the Rocket Lab plan and the risk that one of those three efforts slips up.

title: Rocket Lab, MYR Group, Ameresco, Comfort Systems, and Powell Shares Skyrocket, What You Need To Know
body:
What Happened?

A number of stocks jumped in the morning session after surging capital spending for artificial intelligence infrastructure and defense bolstered demand across power systems, data center construction, and electrical grid buildouts, with gains amplified as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite reached fresh all-time highs.

Capital allocations directed toward artificial intelligence facilities have intensified demand across the industrials sector, as massive computing clusters require extensive power upgrades and physical installations as reported by AP news. Companies providing electrical grid equipment, backup generation, and specialized data center construction are seeing accelerated project orders. Power supply constraints have become a focal challenge for tech infrastructure development, turning industrial suppliers into critical enablers of technology adoption.

Meanwhile, sustained government and corporate budgets for defense modernization provide an additional pillar of predictable revenue. Analysts note that these dual infrastructure drivers have helped insulate power systems and industrial equipment providers from broader macroeconomic cyclicality, reinforcing market momentum as investors anticipate continued multi-year order backlogs across the sector.
